Revenue is in the billions of dollars. Highly recognised across Korea and in Japan's manga market through Piccoma. Valued at about KRW 10 trillion in a 2021 funding round.

Cinemark is one of the largest US movie theater operators, headquartered in Plano, Texas. It operates around 500 theaters and roughly 5,700 screens in the US and Latin America under the Cinemark, Century and Tinseltown names, plus XD premium large-format screens. Customers are moviegoers, and revenue comes from tickets, concessions and advertising, about $3 billion a year. Founded in 1984 and listed on the NYSE (CNK). Strong consumer visibility in North America and Latin America, which are important F1 growth markets, so a plausible partnership or promotion partner.

SM Entertainment is one of South Korea's biggest K-pop entertainment companies, based in Seoul and founded in 1995 by Lee Soo-man. It manages and produces artists such as aespa, NCT, Red Velvet, RIIZE and previously Girls' Generation, EXO and SHINee, and earns from music, concerts, merchandise and content licensing. Listed on KOSDAQ; Kakao became its largest shareholder in 2023. Strong consumer and fan visibility across Asia and globally, and a possible partner for fan-focused F1 content.

Stingray is a Montreal-based music, media and technology company. It operates the Stingray Music streaming and broadcast service for businesses and consumers, plus Stingray Karaoke, Stingray Classica, Djazz and other channels, delivered across cable, satellite, apps and streaming services in over 150 countries. It also supplies in-store music and digital signage, and owns radio stations in Canada. Listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange (RAY.A). Moderate consumer visibility, with B2B in-store music its biggest business.

Smarter Web Company is a UK IT company based in Almondsbury, South Gloucestershire, offering web design, hosting, compliance and content creation services to businesses. It has drawn attention for adding bitcoin to its balance sheet as a treasury strategy in 2025. It is a small company with limited consumer awareness and a modest scale, so a weak sponsorship fit.

about: Spotter is a Los Angeles company providing funding and services to online video creators, famously buying rights to YouTube creators' content libraries and offering advance payments for their future earnings. It also runs creator tools and has worked with large channels. It raised hundreds of millions of dollars in funding, including debt. It has high awareness in the creator economy but is not a mainstream consumer brand.

about: CuriosityStream is a Silver Spring, Maryland factual entertainment streaming company, founded by John Hendricks, the Discovery Channel founder. It offers documentaries on science, nature, history and technology on a subscription service and licenses content to others. It is listed on Nasdaq (CURI) and has several million subscribers via direct and bundled channels. Moderate consumer awareness.

Synchronoss Technologies is a Bridgewater, New Jersey software company providing cloud, messaging and digital experience platforms, such as personal cloud storage white-labelled for telecom carriers like Verizon and AT&T. Customers are mobile operators, with millions of subscribers through them. Founded in 2000 and listed on Nasdaq (SNCR). B2B, with no direct consumer brand recognition.

ADTRAN is a Huntsville, Alabama telecom networking equipment maker, founded in 1986, making broadband access, fiber, Wi-Fi and optical networking equipment and software, sold to telecom operators, cable companies and enterprises. It merged with Germany's ADVA in 2022 and is listed on Nasdaq (ADTN) and in Frankfurt, with revenue around 1 billion dollars. B2B, sponsor of local sports in Huntsville, with little national consumer awareness.

Substack is a San Francisco subscription newsletter publishing platform, founded in 2017, that lets writers, journalists and podcasters send paid newsletters and build audiences, keeping 90 percent of revenue after taking a fee. It hosts millions of paid subscriptions and over 50 million active users. Raised about 200 million dollars, with a 2025 round at a 1.1 billion dollar valuation. Private. Widely known among online readers and writers.

Animaj is a Paris-based children's media and animation company, founded in 2018, that creates animated series and uses AI in production. Its brands include Pocoyo, Treehouse Detectives and Wondermoms, distributed on YouTube and streaming services to young audiences worldwide. It earns advertising and licensing revenue and raised about 175 million euros, including a 2025 investment. Private. Pocoyo is a globally recognized kids' brand, with billions of views.

Corus Entertainment is a Toronto media company that owns specialty TV channels such as Global TV, W Network and Treehouse, radio stations, and children's content producer Nelvana, plus digital businesses. It earns advertising and subscriber revenue, with annual revenue around 1.5 billion Canadian dollars. Controlled by the Shaw family, it is listed on the TSX (CJR.B). It has struggled with debt and declining TV advertising. Well known to Canadian consumers.

Amaze is a Costa Mesa, California creator commerce platform that helps creators and brands build online stores, link pages and sell products to their audiences, including on social media. Customers are creators, influencers and businesses, and it earns subscription and transaction revenue. Funding shown is about 157 million dollars. Private. Moderate awareness among online creators. Ownership and scale are not confirmed from the input.

about: Unrivaled is a professional women's 3-on-3 basketball league founded by WNBA stars Breanna Stewart and Napheesa Collier, with a first season in early 2025 in Miami at Wayfair Arena. It features top WNBA and international players, offseason competition, player ownership stakes and competitive salaries, and earns from media rights, sponsors, tickets and merchandise. It raised about 150 million dollars from investors, with the most recent funding in 2026. Growing sports brand with strong social media reach and appeal to female and younger audiences.

Miaopai is a Chinese short-video sharing and live streaming app, run from Beijing and launched in 2014, with backing from investors such as Sina Weibo, Tencent and Hillhouse, with recorded funding around 775 million dollars. Users upload and view short video clips, and it earns advertising and live-streaming revenue. It was promoted heavily via Weibo, but its position declined against Douyin and Kuaishou. Past mass consumer app in China, now with a reduced position.

about: SoundCloud is a Berlin-based audio streaming platform and music community, founded in 2007, where artists upload and share music, podcasts and audio, and listeners stream it free or through subscription plans (SoundCloud Go). It reportedly has over 300 million tracks and 175 million monthly users, and earns revenue from subscriptions, advertising and artist services (SoundCloud for Artists). It has raised about 540 million dollars from investors and is privately held after a 2024 profit. Strong brand among emerging artists and young listeners.

Guitar Center is a US retailer of musical instruments, based in Westlake Village, California, with about 300 Guitar Center stores and Music & Arts stores, selling guitars, drums, keyboards, DJ gear and pro audio, online and via lessons. Customers are musicians and hobbyists. Revenue is around 2.3 billion dollars. It is privately held by Ares Management after a restructuring in 2020, having been taken private by Bain Capital in 2007. Very recognisable music retail brand in the US.

Harmonic is a San Jose, California video delivery and broadband technology company, selling video processing and delivery software, a cloud-native streaming platform (VOS360), and cable broadband access gear (CableOS) to broadcasters, streaming services and cable operators. Customers include Comcast, Charter and global broadcasters. Revenue is around 700 million dollars. Founded in 1988, it is listed on Nasdaq (HLIT). B2B technology brand with little consumer awareness, though its tech supports live sports streaming.

Beckett Collectibles is a Plano, Texas-based company that publishes price guides for sports cards and collectibles, operates a grading service (Beckett Grading Services), and runs an online marketplace and magazines. It is known as the standard for sports trading card values. Customers are collectors and dealers. Privately held, with recorded funding of 235 million dollars. Strong brand in the sports card hobby, with sports-fan reach.

Wavve is a South Korean streaming service based in Seoul, formed in 2019 through the merger of the Pooq streaming app run by the broadcasters KBS, MBC and SBS with SK Telecom's Oksusu. It provides video on demand, live TV and original content from Korean broadcasters, with a subscription revenue model. Recorded funding is about 250 billion won. Owned by SK Square and the Korean broadcasters. Major Korean streaming brand, though behind Netflix on user numbers.

Anghami is the Arab world's leading music streaming platform, based in Abu Dhabi and founded in Beirut in 2012, with a catalogue of over 100 million songs, podcasts and original Arabic content, and about 120 million registered users. It earns revenue from subscriptions and advertising. It listed on Nasdaq (ANGH) through a SPAC in 2022 and is partly owned by OSN. Strong consumer brand in the Middle East and North Africa.

Bang & Olufsen is a Danish luxury consumer electronics company based in Struer, founded in 1925, making premium televisions, loudspeakers (Beosound), headphones and home audio systems, with high-end design and customers in over 70 countries. Revenue is about 2.5 billion Danish kroner. It is listed on Nasdaq Copenhagen (BO), with Harman among its shareholders, and also licenses its name for Beoplay and car audio. Strong premium consumer brand with recognised design heritage.

Software company behind WordPress.com, WooCommerce, Jetpack, Tumblr, Simplenote and Day One, led by WordPress co-founder Matt Mullenweg. Revenue comes from subscriptions, hosting, commerce plug-ins and enterprise services through WordPress VIP; customers range from bloggers to large publishers. Founded 2005, headquartered in San Francisco with a fully distributed workforce of around 1,900, and valued at about $7.5 billion after a 2021 round. WordPress open-source software runs over 40% of websites. Strong developer and creator brand awareness; ongoing public dispute with WP Engine since 2024.

Former US commercial printing and marketing communications firm headquartered in Stamford, Connecticut, making envelopes, labels, forms, custom packaging and printed marketing materials for businesses. Customers were corporate, publishing and financial clients. Grew by acquisitions and was once a large listed company; filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in February 2018 and its operating businesses were then sold off to other buyers. Funding shown of roughly $1.1 billion reflects debt and equity raised over time. B2B printer with low consumer awareness and no longer operating as before.

Chinese game live-streaming platform based in Guangzhou, where viewers watch esports and gameplay and tip streamers; revenue comes from virtual gifts, subscriptions and advertising. Spun out of YY (now JOYY) and listed on the NYSE (HUYA) in 2018, with Tencent as the largest shareholder. Has tens of millions of monthly active users in China and a growing esports presence. About $1.1 billion in funding shown, largely from a 2020 Tencent-led round. Strong youth and gamer brand in China, little known elsewhere.

Singapore-based digital payments and commerce company behind Codashop and Coda Payments, which let gamers in Southeast Asia and beyond buy in-game currency and top up mobile games and apps using local payment methods. Customers are game publishers and consumers; revenue comes from payment processing and commissions. Founded 2011; raised a large round in 2022 reported at a valuation of around $2.5 billion, with investors including GIC. Codashop is recognisable among mobile gamers in emerging markets; the parent brand is mainly B2B.

about: London technology company that built SpatialOS cloud simulation technology and has pursued virtual worlds, games and defence simulation. Founded 2012 by Herman Narula and Rob Whitehead; SoftBank invested about $500 million in 2017. Sold its defence business to Bohemia Interactive Simulations in 2022 and shifted towards metaverse and gaming projects such as MSquared and M2. Revenue from software licences and services to game studios, governments and enterprises. Total funding shown of about $852 million. Known in the games industry and tech press rather than to consumers.

Nashville, Tennessee, media and entertainment company, shown by Crunchbase as an online platform that offers independent artists tools to reach audiences, tagged with art and media. Total funding of about $730 million is shown, last in April 2022, which is large for such a platform and may reflect a similarly named music business. The brand label also contains OCR noise. about: Irish services company that supports video game developers with art, audio and voice recording, localisation, quality assurance and player support, working on many top-selling games. Operates studios across dozens of countries with over 10,000 staff. Based in Dublin and formerly listed on the London Stock Exchange (KWS); taken private in 2024 by EQT in a deal valuing it at roughly GBP 2.2 billion. Funding shown of about $488 million. B2B gaming brand, known among game studios and investors rather than players.

Canadian cable and telecommunications company, now part of Cogeco Communications (TSX: CCA), providing internet, television and phone services to homes and businesses in Quebec and Ontario, and in the US through its Breezeline brand. Based in Montreal and controlled by the Audet family. Earns subscription revenue from over a million Canadian customers plus several hundred thousand in the US. Funding of about $392 million shown for March 2023, likely debt. Familiar regional consumer brand in Quebec and Ontario.

US digital media company that owns Vox, The Verge, Eater, Polygon, SB Nation, Curbed and New York Magazine, plus podcast and video businesses. Founded in 2003, with offices in Washington, DC and New York. Makes money from advertising, sponsorship, podcasts, commerce and content licensing. Reaches tens of millions of readers a month. Funding of about $408 million shown, last in February 2023, from investors including Comcast and Fox. Strong consumer media brands, particularly among young, tech-savvy US audiences.

Indian media conglomerate behind Zee TV, Zee Cinema, Zee News and other channels, plus the Zee5 streaming service, reaching hundreds of millions of viewers in India and abroad. Headquartered in Mumbai, founded by Subhash Chandra's group and listed on the NSE and BSE (ZEEL). Earns advertising, subscription and content revenue. A planned merger with Sony Pictures Networks India collapsed in 2024. Funding of about $361 million shown for July 2024. Very strong consumer media brand in India, with major cricket and entertainment sponsorship ties.

Broadcast and live production technology company, known for video switchers, cameras, servers and its AMPP cloud-based production platform, used by broadcasters, sports producers and media companies worldwide. Headquartered in Montreal and owned by Black Dragon Capital since 2020 when Belden sold the business. Earns revenue from equipment, software subscriptions and services. Funding of about $256 million shown. Respected B2B brand in broadcasting, with little public consumer awareness.

US movie theatre chain with several hundred cinemas across the country, owned by Cineworld, the UK cinema group which went through Chapter 11 bankruptcy in 2022 to 2023. Based in Knoxville, Tennessee. Earns ticket, concession and advertising revenue and runs the Regal Unlimited rewards programme. Funding of about $250 million shown. Familiar national consumer brand with strong visibility among US moviegoers.

Film and television studio based in Santa Monica, California, behind franchises such as The Hunger Games, John Wick, Saw and Twilight, and TV titles including Mad Men and Orange Is the New Black. Earns money from theatrical releases, streaming licences, TV production and a large film library. Separated from the Starz streaming business in 2025 and is now listed as Lionsgate Studios. The funding figure shown is small relative to its scale. Strong consumer entertainment brand and a plausible partner for activation and content tie-ins.

Brazilian telecom tower company based in Sao Paulo that builds, owns and leases towers and rooftop sites to mobile operators, helping carriers expand coverage. Customers are operators such as the main Brazilian carriers, with revenue from long-term site leases. Funding of about $229 million shown. B2B infrastructure business without consumer brand awareness. Operating across Brazil's large and growing mobile market, it competes with larger tower companies and relies on a small number of carrier customers. Ownership and exact portfolio size should be confirmed before outreach.

about: Italian football club based in Turin, one of Europe's most successful, with a record number of Serie A titles, and owned mainly by Exor, the Agnelli family holding company. Listed on Borsa Italiana (JUVE). Revenue comes from broadcasting, sponsorship, matchday income at Allianz Stadium and player trading, at roughly EUR 450 million a year. Has raised capital in recent years, with funding of about 175 million shown. One of the world's best-known sports brands with a very large global fan base and many commercial partners.

Belgian cinema operator based in Ghent, listed on Euronext Brussels (KIN), known for large multiplex complexes in Belgium, France, Spain, the Netherlands, Luxembourg, Switzerland, Canada and the US, with more than 100 theatres. Earns ticket, food, advertising and property income. Funding of about EUR 160 million shown, likely debt. Strong consumer-facing brand with a reputation for premium screens, and advertising and brand partnerships are part of its business.

Spanish edtech company, based in Madrid, whose Lingokids app teaches English and other skills to children aged 2 to 8 through games, songs and videos. Sells subscriptions to families in the US, Latin America, Spain and elsewhere. Venture-backed. Funding of about $182 million shown. Consumer-facing brand known among parents of young children, with large app download numbers. It reaches families through app stores and school partnerships and offers a free tier with paid upgrades.

Los Angeles film, television and digital production company founded by director and producer Dean Devlin, behind series such as Leverage, The Librarians and Almost Human, and films including Geostorm. Revenue comes from production fees, distribution and licensing. Total funding of about $170 million shown, probably production financing. A mid-sized creative business well known in Hollywood, with modest public brand awareness.

Deep-tech B2B brand known in automotive sensor circles, with no public consumer awareness yet. It is an early-stage company, and little is public about production timelines or partners, so any contact would be about technology and automotive supply rather than brand sponsorship.
